first.rationale: Objective is sustainable long-term QUALIFIED revenue, so triage targets the two inherited beliefs that are most decision-critical and whose recorded endpoints are weakest proxies for that objective. memory_73 (promotional pricing) is the emotionally obvious response to the competitor's entry pricing and would be the largest, hardest-to-reverse commitment; its record cites acquisition and revenue lift but says nothing about retention, margin, or cohort quality, so 'strong lift' may be discount-driven churn-prone volume. Verifying it is the cheapest way to avoid a costly mistake and to know whether to abandon my current plan. memory_31 is the direct evidentiary basis for the action I intend: it justifies cutting required signup fields, but its endpoint is first-week activation, a proxy that can move opposite to qualified revenue if removing fields degrades lead routing and qualification. I need the original record to know whether revenue or lead-quality was measured at all, and which fields were cut. I did not verify memory_86 (it corroborates the same direction through a lower-risk mechanism — shortening flow rather than removing qualifying data — and if memory_31 fails, memory_86 still supports a field-preserving variant), nor memory_57 (already records a revenue-and-retention endpoint, so it is better supported for this objective), nor memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist is not the constraint this week; the observed declines are self-serve activation and onboarding). Current intent: simplify_onboarding, because it is the only candidate that directly addresses both observed declines (onboarding -4%, activation -6%) at their shared upstream cause rather than buying volume that must still pass through a leaking funnel — fixing the funnel also raises the return on any later pricing or referral push. Scale is a small guarded test, not a broad rollout: the supporting evidence is 45-64 days old, measured on proxy metrics, and predates both the competitor's entry and the current declines, so the inherited lift may no longer replicate. Guardrails: preserve or shadow-collect qualifying fields, and instrument lead-quality and downstream conversion-to-qualified-revenue, not just activation rate, so an activation gain bought with worse lead quality is detected rather than celebrated. All conclusions remain provisional pending the two archive pulls; if memory_31's record shows no revenue or quality endpoint, I will run the memory_86 field-preserving variant instead, and if memory_73's record shows durable margin-positive retention I will reconsider pricing.

final.rationale: The two pulls resolved exactly the questions that mattered. memory_73 is now disconfirmed for this objective: exp_73's +18% qualified revenue came with -12% 30-day retention, i.e. the acquired cohort does not survive first renewal, and the source record explicitly warns against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable growth. That removes promotional_pricing from consideration despite it being the intuitive answer to the competitor's entry pricing — matching a discount war would buy exactly the cohort exp_73 showed evaporates, and would burn the one slot on the least durable option. memory_31 is confirmed and, importantly, confirmed on the right endpoint: signup +15%, activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, retention -1%. The revenue lift is real but modest and the retention effect is slightly negative, so this is a genuine but small win, not a windfall. The record also carries an explicit scope limit — holds on SMB, not replicated on other segments — so I am scoping the experiment to SMB self-serve and not generalizing beyond it. Decision: simplify_onboarding, SMB-scoped, standard experiment. Rationale for direction: it is the only candidate that addresses the shared upstream cause of both observed declines (onboarding -4%, activation -6%) rather than pushing more volume through a leaking funnel, and it is corroborated by memory_86 through an independent mechanism (shortening flow) and complemented by memory_91 (in-product activation nudges) if a follow-on slot opens. Rationale for scale: standard rather than broad, because the supporting evidence is 64 days old, predates both the competitor's entry and the current declines, and the -1% retention signal means the effect is not unambiguously free. A broad rollout would over-commit on a +4% revenue effect measured under different market conditions. Guardrails carried forward: preserve or shadow-collect qualifying fields rather than deleting them, and instrument conversion-to-qualified-revenue and 30-day retention alongside activation, so that a repeat of the exp_73 failure mode — a proxy metric rising while cohort quality falls — is detected rather than celebrated. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving with this slot: whether the current activation decline is caused by funnel friction at all or by the competitor changing the mix of who signs up. If the SMB test reproduces well below +4%, that mix hypothesis becomes the leading explanation and the next slot should go to segment-level diagnosis, not to another funnel tweak. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) remains plausible but unverified and off-target for the observed self-serve declines; referral_incentive (memory_57) already carries a retention-inclusive endpoint and is the strongest fallback if onboarding work underperforms.
